clue.text: "Cheers!" and "Shame!" said to be unacceptable

indicators.note: said tells us the two exclamations are to be heard, giving a spelling that only sounds like them

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks and boo a jeer of disapproval; together they make a word heard here

explanation.surface: Raising a toast and booing at the same time is said to be bad manners.
explanation.walkthrough: TABU is a variant spelling of taboo; 'ta' is British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is forbidden by social custom, so it is not acceptable to mention or do.

clue.text: Someone may not care that Good Samaritan paid it

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the trifling sum in the phrase not to care ...
second meaning: in the parable the Samaritan paid the innkeeper ... to look after the injured man

explanation.walkthrough: Luke's parable says the Samaritan took out two pence (denarii) and gave them to the host; 'not care twopence' means not care at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Twopence is both a proverbially worthless amount and the coins the Samaritan handed over.

clue.text: British surgeon's finding skin problems

parts.note: Joseph Lister was the British surgeon who pioneered antiseptic surgery

explanation.surface: A British surgeon diagnosing complaints of the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Blisters are bubbles of fluid under the skin, common minor dermatological complaints.

clue.text: A French girl with Parisian father, daughter not spoilt

parts.note: un is the French word for a
Pam is a girl's name
père is French for father, as a Parisian would say

explanation.surface: A French girl and her father and daughter, none of them pampered.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper is to indulge or spoil, so one never pampered has not been spoilt.

clue.text: Granny is being kept inside for a month

indicators.note: being kept inside means the word is goes within the granny

parts.note: nan is a familiar name for a grandmother
taken as written

explanation.surface: Grandma stuck indoors for a whole month.
explanation.definitionFit: Nisan is the first month of the Jewish religious calendar, in spring.

clue.text: Song involving duo — it excited parts of concert-halls

indicators.note: involving means the song wraps around the other letters

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to be rearranged
taken as written, joining duo in the jumble

explanation.surface: A duet aria that thrilled the audience in the concert hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditoria, the Latin plural of auditorium, are the seating areas where an audience listens.

clue.text: Perhaps we bond, providing definitive ruling

parts.note: we is an example of a pronoun, the perhaps marking it as one instance
cement binds things together

explanation.surface: We may unite, if an authoritative ruling is given.
explanation.definitionFit: A pronouncement is a formal or authoritative declaration or judgment.

clue.text: In old city taking time off is fellow traveller

indicators.note: in places the fellow within the city's remaining letters
taking a letter off means removing it, here from the start of the old city
off completes taking off: removing a letter

parts.note: Troy is the ancient city of Homer's Iliad
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A wanderer in an ancient city, taking time off.
explanation.definitionFit: Romany people are a traditionally nomadic ethnic group, often called travellers in Britain.

clue.text: Ultimately saddled with university restrictions and obligations

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word saddled

parts.note: its final letter is the one taken
ties are things that bind or restrict

explanation.surface: Finally burdened with campus rules and responsibilities.
explanation.definitionFit: Duties are tasks one is bound to perform, moral or legal obligations.

clue.text: Old illicit traders disposing of the last of their drugs

indicators.note: disposing of something gets rid of it, so a letter is dropped from the traders

parts.note: pirates sell illegal copies of goods, so they are illicit traders

indicators.note: the last of points to the final letter of the word their

parts.note: its final letter is the one disposed of

explanation.surface: Former smugglers getting rid of the remainder of their narcotics stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Opiates are narcotic drugs derived from opium, such as morphine and heroin.

clue.text: Have me prattle inordinately, getting the last word in — too excitable?

indicators.note: getting a word in puts it inside the jumbled letters
in completes getting in: placing one thing inside another
inordinately means excessively, beyond order, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to be jumbled
taken as written, the rest of the jumbled letters
amen is the word said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: Someone who chatters excessively and insists on the final say may be overexcitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Have' is a link word here; the anagram is of 'me prattle' only.
explanation.definitionFit: A temperamental person is moody and liable to sudden emotional outbursts.

clue.text: Party men approaching dull person easily put upon

indicators.note: approaching means the party and men come up next to the following piece, joining it in order

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
OR, other ranks, are the ordinary soldiers rather than officers
mat (or matt) describes a finish without shine

explanation.surface: Partygoers drifting toward a boring guest who lets everyone walk over him.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, often clued as men.
explanation.definitionFit: A doormat is literally wiped by feet, so figuratively a submissive person others take advantage of.

clue.text: Cafe and store to be installed in piece of land shortly

indicators.note: being installed in something means being placed within it, so the store goes inside
shortly means cut short, so the final letter of the land goes

parts.note: an estate is a large area of land
a mine is a store or rich supply, as in a mine of information

explanation.surface: A café and a shop going up on a small plot.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French café or bar, a word picked up by British soldiers in the First World War.

clue.text: Cat to come back, wanting bit of breakfast

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is missing from the rebound word

parts.note: to bounce is to spring back after hitting something

indicators.note: a bit of the word breakfast is its opening letter

parts.note: its opening letter is the bit that goes missing

explanation.surface: A pet cat returning home, missing part of its morning meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big wild feline of Central Asia.

clue.text: Burrowing insect having one grumble, to penetrate a set of books

parts.note: to carp is to complain about trivial things
to enter something is to go into it
taken as written
the New Testament is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An insect that, with a complaint, bores into a shelf of volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: NT is the New Testament, a common crossword shorthand for a set of books.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpenter ants are large ants that excavate galleries in wood to nest, hence burrowing.

clue.text: Fashioning the end bit with circular sealant

parts.note: a tail is the end part of something
an O-ring is a circular rubber seal used in machinery

explanation.surface: Finishing off a job by fitting a round seal at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailoring is the craft of making clothes, giving them shape and fashion.

clue.text: Team row? It could be a distraction

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
a line is a row

explanation.surface: A squabble within the team may distract it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel; here it is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideline is a secondary activity pursued alongside one's main job, diverting attention.

clue.text: Group with old people getting dressed

parts.note: a band is a group
aged means old

explanation.surface: A group of elderly people putting their clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed' looks like clothed; here it means having had a wound dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound dressed with a bandage is bandaged.

clue.text: Wild animal eating bit of tough heather in specific region

indicators.note: eating means the animal swallows a letter, holding it inside
wild suggests the letters of the animal run riot into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: bit of picks out the opening letter of tough

parts.note: only its opening letter is eaten
erica is the botanical genus of heathers

explanation.surface: A wild creature munching tough heather on its own patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin America is the part of the Americas where Romance languages are spoken, a particular geographical area.

clue.text: Female, feeble soul initially, burns brightly

parts.note: lame means weak or unconvincing, as a lame excuse

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word soul

parts.note: only its opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A weak-spirited woman who nevertheless blazes with passion at first.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire that flames gives off bright tongues of burning gas.

clue.text: Season starting late, November, for US student

indicators.note: starting late means the word begins after its first letter, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: winter is a season

explanation.surface: A term beginning late in November for an American student.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US an intern is an advanced medical student or recent graduate in hospital training.

clue.text: Some hospital ungenerously making charge

indicators.note: some of the words means only a portion of their letters is taken, running across the gap

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of hospital and the start of ungenerously

explanation.surface: A hospital mean enough to bill its patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' suggests a fee; here it is a sudden attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden forward thrust or rush at someone, a charge.

clue.text: Those people joining cricket side stop improving

indicators.note: joining means the pieces are attached to one another in order

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field
them refers to those people
to end is to stop

explanation.surface: Some people join a cricket team and then quit while improving.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on (leg) side is the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: On the mend is an idiom for recovering from illness, getting better.

clue.text: Fat man's folds

definitions.meaning: first meaning: belonging to Friar Tuck, the portly friar of Robin Hood legend
second meaning: flat folds sewn into fabric

explanation.walkthrough: Friar Tuck is the stout, jolly friar in Robin Hood's band.
explanation.definitionFit: Tucks are stitched pleats in cloth, and the possessive of Tuck is spelled the same when the apostrophe goes.

clue.text: Female to take off clothes endlessly for great men?

parts.note: Mae is a woman's name, as in the actress Mae West

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the undressing word is cut off

parts.note: to strip is to undress

explanation.surface: A woman stripping without stopping, aimed at impressing important men.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that maestri are masters of music, not simply great men.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri is the Italian plural of maestro, an eminent conductor or master of an art.

clue.text: Keen to provide something for future growth

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a piece snipped from a plant to root and grow anew

explanation.walkthrough: Keen reads as eager here, but it means sharp; the gardener's sense is the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardeners propagate plants from a cutting, and a keen edge or comment is described as cutting.

clue.text: I am an expert on the Chinese lingo — it's so complicated

definitions.text: I am an expert on the Chinese
definitions.note: the definition speaks as the expert in the first person, standing for a noun naming that person

indicators.note: complicated means the letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to be rearranged
taken as written, its apostrophe ignored
taken as written, the last of the jumbled letters

explanation.surface: A scholar admitting the Chinese language is very difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinologist is a scholar who studies China, its language, history and culture.

clue.text: Drop live commercial

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
an ad is a commercial advertisement
